THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation passed by the II Addl.
Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC.No.292/2011 dated 25.05.2015.
2. Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for both parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Claims Tribunal.

4. The brief facts of the case are:
On 6.4.2010 the petitioner on a Two Wheeler bike bearing Regn. No. KA. 32/R-8926 as a pillion rider along with his family friend Rizwan Ahmed who was riding the bike were proceeding towards Gulbarga from Bhagodi at that time a Tractor bearing Regn.

No.KA.32/T-1476-1477 from opposite side at Bhankur cross with high speed and in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle, due to which the petitioner and bike rider fell down and sustained grievous Injuries and he was shifted to Govt.
Hospital, Gulbarga
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he has been permanently disabled and lost source of income.
Thereby causing dent to him financially, mentally and physically.
Hence, he preferred a claim petition seeking compensation.
5. After service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared and filed written statement denying the contents of claim made by the petitioner and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.

sentences.text: Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal after considering the notional monthly income of the claimant awarded compensation of Rs.69,010/-.
8. Being aggrieved by the quantum of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the present appeal is filed.
9. The learned counsel for the claimant contended that having regard to the nature of the injuries sustained by the claimant, the Tribunal ought to have awarded adequate compensation.

He further submits that the tribunal has not passed any compensation toward laid up period, loss of amenities,
attendant charges so also the tribunal has awarded meager compensation towards loss of future income, pain and suffering.
On all these grounds sought for allowing the appeal and consequently seeks to enhance the compensation.
10. Per contra, the learned counsel for the insurer supported the judgment and award of the Tribunal and therefore contended that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal be not disturbed.
11. It is seen that the respondents had not challenged the judgment and award and therefore accepted the liability to pay the compensation.

Insofar as claim for compensation is concerned,
injuries show that petitioner had suffered permanent disability.

12. A perusal of the impugned judgment at paragraph No.21 and 22 wherein the tribunal has observed as under;
"21. Loss of Future Income:

As per the evidence of petitioner he was working as Carpenter earlier to the accident and was earning Rs.5,000/- per month and Rs.50/-
per day for Bhatta but except his evidence no other material is produced to prove the said fact and as per the evidence of Doctor there is 10% disability but cross-examination of this PW.2 discloses that he is not treated doctor but he has only examined the petitioner for the purpose of issuing disability certificate and it was suggested to doctor that the disability to the whole body will be 1/4th %.
If the percentage of disability is 10% to the Injured part of the body.
So, if we consider this fact then the percentage of disability may be 2 or 3 %.
So, if we consider the disability at 3% in the absence of any document to prove the age of the petitioner.

As per injury certificate the age of the petitioner is 35 years is to be taken into account and regarding the income of the petitioner it is feasible to consider Rs.100/- per day as his income as the accident has taken place in the year 2010.
So, monthly income of the petitioner would be Rs.3,000/- and annual income comes to Rs.36,000/-.

So, in the absence of any other documentary evidence, the said age is to be taken into consideration for applying multiplier then the age of the petitioner is 35 years the multiplier applicable is 16 as per the case law reported in Sarla Varma and others V/S Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

sentences.text: Annual Income Rs.36,000/- x 3% Disability which comes to Rs.1,080/-.
If the said amount of Rs. 1,080/- is multiplied by multiplier 16, it would be Rs.17,280/-.

22. Loss of Marriage Prospects: No amount is awarded towards this heading as the petitioner himself has stated in his petition that he is having wife and children.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.15,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs.36,730/-
3. Loss of future Rs.17,280/-
income Total Rs.69,010/-

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.69,010/- which is to be rounded off to Rs.69,000/- along with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

13. PW.2-Dr.Vijay Rathod, who has examined the petitioner clinically and found the fracture of first rib on left side, fracture of 1st and 2nd rib on right side and fracture of mandible of right side,
tenderness present in left chest over first and second ribs and left shoulder pain, X-ray report shows the evidence of old fracture.

Considering the nature of injuries, the tribunal assessed the disability only at 3% which needs to be enhanced in view of pain of left shoulder at 5% and difficulty in deep breathing at 5% the total disability would be 10%.
Hence, it is just and proper to assess disability at 5% instead of 3% assessed by the tribunal.

14. Considering the nature of injuries and medical evidence, I am of the considered opinion that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be re-determined and re- calculated as under:-
Rs.6,000 x 12 x 16 X 5% = 57,600 which is rounded off to Rs.58,000/-.

sentences.text:
In view of the above, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER (a) The appeal is allowed in part.
(b) The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC.No.292/2011 dated 25.05.2015 is modified.
The compensation of Rs.69,010/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.1,40,800/-.
(c) The respondent-No.2-insurer is liable to pay the compensation to the claimant along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
(d) The respondent No.2-insurer is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
(e) All other terms and conditions stipulated by the Tribunal shall stand intact.
